newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's ailing Lada-maker sees output rising.
newsitem.headline: Russia's ailing Lada-maker sees output rising.

text.p: Russia's heavily-indebted car maker AvtoVAZ plans to boost output to 680,000 cars this year, above 654,000 initially planned, and to raise it further in 1997 to 701,000, the company said on Tuesday.

AvtoVAZ chief spokesman Vladimir Isakov told Reuters the plant, where Lada and Niva cars are made, was working normally in spite of mounting debts to the state budget, public sectors and suppliers totalling about 10 trillion roubles ($1.8 billion).
"Car-making is perfectly organised, output is rising, sales are up, there are no strikes. The problem is that current tax payments and debt repayment eat up all of our profits," Isakov said.
He said this year's output would exceed the average annual production over the past five years. An additional 7,000 Lada kits would be sent to Finland for assembly this year.
By the end of November AvtoVAZ produced more than 620,000 cars. October sales of 69,000 cars were a record, Isakov said.
"There are no cars stored in our backyard, everything is being sold immediately," he said.
The government warned AvtoVAZ last month it could start bankruptcy procedures against it. The company was forced to promise to double its share capital and offer new shares to investors.

"The bankruptcy talk is totally a matter for the government's conscience. We cannot be blamed for the break-up of links within the former Soviet Union, rouble depreciation and higher taxes," Isakov said.

AvtoVAZ is Russia's eighth biggest company by sales and its fifth biggest employer. The company has a poor history of management and marketing and the boxy Ladas are popular for their availability rather than quality.
